title: HR Agency overview
description: Runtime, HTTP, SQL, messaging, event store and feeds of one HR Agency service.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: Process CPU time / CPU cores available to the container (all of the machine's cores - the compose file sets no cpu limit).

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: Working set / container memory limit (mem_limit: 512m) read from cgroup.

panels.title: GC Heap
panels.description: Managed heap size (all generations) after the last GC.

panels.title: Threads
panels.description: Thread pool threads.

panels.title: Instances
panels.description: Instances that sent telemetry in the last minute. Services push over OTLP, so there is no scrape target per service - an instance that stops sending drops to 0 here.

panels.title: Health checks
panels.description: The /health/ready checks, run every 30 s by the health check publisher and exported as hr_health_status (1 healthy, 0.5 degraded, 0 unhealthy).

targets.expr: max by (service_name, service_version, deployment_environment_name, telemetry_sdk_version, service_instance_id) (target_info{job="$job"})

panels.title: HTTP (API, file service, reports service, job board)
Requests total
panels.description: In the selected time range.

panels.title: Latency P50 / P95 / P99  (dots = exemplars -> click to open the trace)
panels.description: Exemplars carry trace_id. Hover a dot and use 'Open trace in Rootprint'.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, http_request_method, http_route, http_response_status_code) (rate(http_server_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="$job",http_route!~"/health.*|/metrics"}[$__range])))

panels.title: Outgoing HTTP calls / sec by target
panels.description: What this service calls: the file service, the reports service, RustFS, the API (from the job board). The telemetry exporter's own calls are left out.

panels.title: PostgreSQL (Npgsql client metrics) - server side on the PostgreSQL dashboard
DB latency P50 / P95 / P99 (with exemplars)
Messaging (Wolverine) - broker and queues on the RabbitMQ dashboard
Handled / sec
panels.description: Messages this service's handlers finished, local queues and RabbitMQ alike.

panels.title: Failed (range)
panels.description: Handler exceptions. A retry that later succeeds still counts once here.

panels.title: Sent / sec
panels.description: Cascaded and published messages - to local queues and to x.emails.

panels.title: Outbox
panels.description: Envelopes waiting in the durable outbox. Growing = the broker does not take them.

panels.title: Scheduled
panels.description: Scheduled envelopes, e.g. password reset timeouts waiting for their moment.

panels.title: Effective time P95
panels.description: From sending a message to its handler finishing - queue wait included.

panels.title: Execution time P95 by message type
panels.description: Time inside the handler alone.

panels.title: Events appended / sec by type (top 15)
panels.description: marten.event.append - every new event type is counted without code (TrackEventCounters).

panels.title: Events processed by projections / sec
panels.description: The async daemon catching up. Read models are eventually consistent - this is how eventual.

panels.title: Projection gap (events behind, average)
panels.description: How far behind the high water mark a projection was when it picked up a batch. A projection whose gap only grows has stopped - look for its error in Rootprint logs.

targets.expr: sum by (projection) (rate(label_replace({__name__=~"marten_.*_all_gap_sum", job="hr-api"}, "projection", "$1", "__name__", "marten_(.*)_all_gap_sum")[5m:15s])) / sum by (projection) (rate(label_replace({__name__=~"marten_.*_all_gap_count", job="hr-api"}, "projection", "$1", "__name__", "marten_(.*)_all_gap_count")[5m:15s]))

panels.title: Feed failures (range)
panels.description: Each failure is also logged with its organization - Rootprint: service hr-feeds-worker, severity Error.

panels.title: Largest feed
panels.description: Average size of a generated file - a feed that only grows is a post that never closes.

options.content:
1. **Spot the anomaly** here - 5xx, a P95 spike, DB failures, handler failures, a projection falling behind. Pick the service in **Service** at the top.
2. **Open a trace**: on a *Latency* / *DB latency* chart hover an exemplar dot → **Open trace in Rootprint**, or go to [Rootprint → Traces](http://localhost:8282/traces) and filter by service (`hr-api`, `hr-file-service`, `hr-notification-worker`, ...).
3. The waterfall shows **HTTP request → Wolverine handler → PostgreSQL / file service / RabbitMQ publish**, and a mail continues in `hr-notification-worker` under the same trace id.
4. **Logs**: [Rootprint → Logs](http://localhost:8282/) - `trace_id:<id>`, `severity_text:Error`, `attributes.OrganizationId:<id>` (every request log carries the tenant). A 4xx/5xx response body carries the same `traceId`.
5. Deeper: **Emails worker**, **File service**, **RabbitMQ**, **PostgreSQL** dashboards (links at the top).

Traffic: `./infrastructure/start.sh --traffic | --emails | --files | --job-board` (k6 scripts in `k6/`).
